scenes.summary: You meet Crowe and Ardelia. Crowe shares his idea with you. He wants Clavell and Dean to truly act on their own this time, instead of relying on help from other people.

lines.text: Ah, my friends from Endfield. You're here.
We received your message and came to check on the ⟦key|geological probe's⟧ progress. But ... the entire work site appears somewhat ... disorganized.
That's primarily because ... probe construction is just one step away from completion. However, we have yet to verify the parameter set and data samples of the surveillance unit...
The entire crew is exhausted by the task...
What about Dean and Clavell?
They ... started arguing first. People got them to cool off before moving on with their jobs.
I knew it.
The two boys learned nothing from their experiences and made a fool of themselves. They deserve it.
Nevertheless, we should try to fix the problems with our surveillance unit.
Don't worry, Supervisor. If the sitch gets out of control, I'll step in and get it fixed. But now, I don't intend to interfere or help them out of their mess.
So you actually know how to get everything done! Then ... why would you just sit around and let them mess things up?
I actually want to let them achieve spectacular success on their own! But look at 'em! Can they pull it off?
My generation was built different. Some of us got back from the frontlines to work floors that had no materials. We ended up making our own equipment by taking parts off the lathe.
This generation has a serious problem. They bicker and complain. They don't know how to work as a team. Worse, they strut around with a sense of useless pride.
Hrrrmph. I would have taken care of this on my own if I were younger. I wouldn't even need two inept fools of apprentices to take care of this job.
The way you said that really sounds like a Shifu we had in Tanjian Hall...
Hmph. But ... they'll be running Valley IV one day.
This disaster really changed me as well...
Young people like you will be running the show. We even changed the Utjug Order. No matter how hard we try, I guess it's time to pass on the baton.
The apprentices may have plenty of issues, but they are gifted in their own right.
That said, they must learn to solve problems on their own. If another disaster like the last one strikes again, they'll have no one to count on.
Ah, what I meant by young people doesn't include you, Endmin. You're a legend...
However, the UWST needs promising youths to shoulder the burden of the ⟦key|United Syndicates⟧.
I hope they will appreciate all the work you've put in for them.
Them? Appreciate my work? Well, just sit around. They'll be crying for help soon enough.
They neglected too many details. The first activation of the probe will involve a certain degree of danger... But I didn't remind them this time.
Aren't you worried about accidents?
Don't worry. I won't risk this if human safety is involved. Since the Endmin is with us, we can afford to wait before giving them help. Let them have a taste of their mistakes and learn from it.
Fine... I understand what you're trying to do.

options: The young people you're talking about......

r: The young people you're talking about......

scenes.summary: You find Dean mid-adjustment of the surveillance unit's core parameters, only to be thwarted by sudden mechanical failure. You decide to help them.

lines.text: Endmin! You're here! We got a ... um, situation.
There's a minor hiccup with several key parameters of the surveillance unit...
So, my friend here used a set of temporary data that messed up our control group. We gotta reset the surveillance unit to its default state.
Ah... yeah, that's right. But the machine is now malfunctioning. Repairing it will take a while, but I heard about the Endmin's ⟦key|Originium Arts⟧...
No problem. Endmin, we can lend them our assistance.
Great. These parameters should work now...
We finally got it done. Wait. What's that noise?
What is this trembling...?
Oh dear. Get out!

scenes.summary: The pair report a new issue. The biological specimen chamber has malfunctioned, and the currently stored samples are contaminated. You decide to help out.

lines.text: Hooo... Thank you, my Endfielder friends.
I'm so glad nobody's hurt! Oh! The machine...! Phew... The machine looks fine ... and the parameter set looks right as well.
We ... actually need help with one more thing.
We got a few problems with the ⟦key|bio samples⟧ required for the surveillance. We found a ⟦key|replacement⟧, but the sample bin...

I'll just lay it straight — we got the wrong bio samples. The sample bin is down and can't be activated. It has an independent operation scheme, and the inner workings are pretty intricate. We can't simply take it all apart.
So, Endmin ... we might need your help to put the samples into the bin...
I understand. The Endmin will help.
Great!
Alright. The samples are finally... Wait. What's that noise?
WHOAH!
The new samples are effective... Oh, we finally made it.
That was close... Thank goodness the device is undamaged.
Let me check the results...

scenes.summary: Dean and Clavell start arguing about the crisis they faced earlier. Crowe appears, gives them a harsh lesson, and assigns various jobs to them. Everyone then decides to activate the geological probe together.

lines.text: Wow. This actually looks super impressive. You two turned out to be pretty professional at this.
We wouldn't have been in that mess if we'd had proper samples.
What? You're the one who messed up the parameters.
I reminded you that the testing environment of the samples might change. And I could totally fix the parameter issues on my own.
And you're blaming me? I was the one who helped you churn out those parameters!
Well, you promised that you'd find some proper samples. In the end, it was my replacements that solved the crisis!
Why you...
Hold on, what's happening...? The ⟦key|geological probe⟧ isn't doing anything.
What?! Let me see! ...What by Talos is wrong this time?
This isn't supposed to happen... Strange. Why? How?
Endmin...
ENOUGH! Both of you! Can't believe you're still asking others to take care of your problems!!
Professor Crowe ... I ... it wasn't like that...
Done explaining already, Dean? It's been years and you never bothered changing that unruly personality of yours!

You're always rushing straight into things without thinking about the consequences. True, you might get rewarded if things work, but the losses are just as great. Consider yourself lucky if we only take property damage, because the way you do things has a chance of inflicting serious injuries!
You can't bear the losses. No one can. You gotta learn how to smash the brakes before you actually hurt somebody!
You're right, Professor...
And you. Don't just stand there and gawk.
I'm sorry...

There are times when Dean is actually right. You gotta take a bold step forward in scientific research. You can't make progress by dancing around in circles. No one can predict what we'll be looking at in the future. And no one can solve everything with the same old ways!
Be cautious when you need it. But when you need to be bold, do not hesitate. Windows of opportunity can disappear in an instant.
I've learned my lesson...

I appointed the two of you to lead the geological probe construction project *because* I want you to help each other out. You two should be covering for each other's deficiencies. Alone, you might slip — but together, you should be able to figure it out.

I thought you learned something from the disaster, but what did I see? Boys who won't stop bickering, who go running off to the Endmin for help. This is the final stage and you still want others to clean up your mess. How am I supposed to let you lead the reconstruction of Valley IV?
Professor Crowe...
You're lucky you still got me and the Endmin around to sort out your blighted mistakes. But what about next time? If you run into another disaster of this scale, who are you going to turn to?

I've submitted applications to assign you to the ⟦key|Originium Power Plant⟧. You'll be taking over my job, and that of old Daniels. No one will be around to help you, and you won't be getting any lessons from anyone.
Wait...! Professor Crowe... What about you?
We can't do without you, Professor Crowe!
Just look at you sorry lot. How am I supposed to hand over the mission of rebuilding Valley IV? I only have six more years to go. Don't let me catch you stirring up trouble again!
But... Okay!
We'll ... we'll make full use of these six years!
Hmph. Follow me. There's still the final step for constructing the geological probe. The crew really worked hard for this. Don't keep them waiting.

scenes.summary: The large geological probe formally activates. A new phase has begun for the reconstruction project. Everyone talks casually about the future.

lines.text: Wow! It's moving!
The ⟦key|geological probe⟧ will constantly release various isotopes, sound waves, and penetrants underground. The data we gather will help scientists speed up the healing of the local ecology.
I'm really looking forward to seeing this place restored to its former glory. When we first arrived at the Power Plateau, the place was already in ruins.
That's a real shame. The Plateau used to be a scenic location.
Don't worry. We'll do our best and make the Plateau more beautiful than ever before.
Mmmh! With time, the land will slowly rejuvenate and remediate itself.
Mr. Crowe, how do you think Valley IV might change in the future?
How do I think? If these young people are in charge, the future looks bleak!
But ... no matter what happens, it's the youths who'll be building the future. I myself want to see Valley IV getting better...
If the people in the Valley live stable and secure lives, that'd be good enough for me.
Perhaps it won't be long before these young people start to impress you. Right, Professor?
Hahahaha! I sure hope so! But the future of Talos-II ... now that will be decided by you, Endfielders!
